questions.stem: A line passes through the points \((0, 4)\) and \((3, 10)\). Which of the following is the equation of the line?
questions.explanation:
Use the slope formula with the two given points \((0, 4)\) and \((3, 10)\).
$$m = \frac{10 - 4}{3 - 0} = \frac{6}{3} = 2$$
Since the line passes through \((0, 4)\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(4\). The equation of the line is \(y = 2x + 4\).

questions.stem: Which of the following values of \(x\) satisfies \(3x - 7 > 2\)?
questions.explanation:
Solve the inequality for \(x\).
$$\begin{aligned}3x - 7 &> 2 \\ 3x &> 9 \\ x &> 3\end{aligned}$$
The solution is \(x > 3\). Of the choices, only \(x = 4\) satisfies this condition. Note that \(x = 3\) does not work because the inequality is strict (\(>\), not \(\geq\)).

questions.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(x^2 + 6x + 5\) and reveals the minimum value of the expression?
questions.explanation:
Complete the square to rewrite the expression in vertex form.
$$\begin{aligned}x^2 + 6x + 5 &= x^2 + 6x + 9 - 9 + 5 \\ &= (x + 3)^2 - 4\end{aligned}$$
The expression \((x+3)^2 - 4\) reveals that the minimum value is \(-4\), occurring when \(x = -3\) (since \((x+3)^2 \geq 0\) for all real \(x\)).

questions.stem: In triangle \(ABC\), the measure of angle \(A\) is \(3x°\), the measure of angle \(B\) is \((2x + 20)°\), and the measure of angle \(C\) is \((x + 10)°\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(B\)?
questions.explanation:
The sum of the angles in any triangle is \(180°\). Set up and solve an equation.
$$\begin{aligned}3x + (2x + 20) + (x + 10) &= 180 \\ 6x + 30 &= 180 \\ 6x &= 150 \\ x &= 25\end{aligned}$$
Substitute \(x = 25\) to find angle \(B\): \(2(25) + 20 = 70°\).

questions.stem: A data analyst researching the demand for ferry tickets in a certain city recorded ferry ticket sales for 31 days. On August 31, there were 851 ferry tickets sold. The percent decrease in the number of ferry tickets sold from August 1 to August 31 was 8%. How many ferry tickets were sold on August 1?
questions.explanation:
This is a percent decrease of an unknown original value. Translate the information from words to an equation to solve. \(851\) is tickets sold after an \(8\)% decrease from the another amount of tickets sold, so the equation is \(851=x-.08x)
$$\begin{aligned} 851=.92x \\ x=\frac{851}{.92) &= 925 \end{aligned}$$

questions.stem: Line \(l\) is defined by the equation \(4x + 2y = 10\). Line \(m\) is perpendicular to line \(l\) in the \(xy\)-plane. What is the slope of line \(m\)?
questions.explanation:
Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form \(y = mx + b\).
$$\begin{aligned}4x + 2y &= 10 \\ 2y &= -4x + 10 \\ y &= -2x + 5\end{aligned}$$
The slope of line \(l\) is \(-2\), so the slope of perpendicular line \(m\) is the negative reciprocal, or \(\frac{1}{2}\).

questions.stem: A circle in the \(xy\)-plane has a diameter with endpoints \((-1,-8)\) and \((-1,4)\). An equation for this circle is \((x+1)^2+(y+2)^2=r^2)\), where \(r\) is a positive constant. What is the value of \(r\)?
questions.explanation:
The question asks for the value of \(r\). In the equation \((x+1)^2+(y+2)^2=r^2\), \(r\) represents the radius of the circle, so this problem asks you to find the radius of the circle.
The radius is half the length of the diameter. The given endpoints share the same \(x\)-coordinate, so the diameter is simply the vertical distance between them.
$$d = 4-(-8) = 12 \implies r = \frac{12}{2} = 6$$

questions.stem: A recreation center offers swimming classes and dance classes. Last Tuesday, 3 swimming classes and 1 dance class were held, with a total of 49 participants. Last Wednesday, 1 swimming class and 2 dance classes were held, with a total of 38 participants. Each class of the same type had the same number of participants. How many participants attended each swimming class?
questions.explanation:
Let \(s\) = number of participants in each swimming class and \(d\) = number of participants in each dance class.
$$\begin{aligned}3s + d &= 49 \\ s + 2d &= 38\end{aligned}$$
From the first equation, \(d = 49 - 3s\). Substitute into the second equation.
$$\begin{aligned}s + 2(49 - 3s) &= 38 \\ s + 98 - 6s &= 38 \\ -5s &= -60 \\ s &= 12\end{aligned}$$
Each swimming class had \(12\) participants.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3}\) for \(x \neq 3\). For what value of \(x\) does \(f(x) = 10\)?
questions.explanation:
First simplify \(f(x)\) by factoring the numerator.
$$f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} = \frac{(x+3)(x-3)}{x-3} = x + 3$$
Now set \(f(x) = 10\) and solve.
$$x + 3 = 10 \implies x = 7$$

questions.stem:
$$\dfrac{3m}{4n} = \dfrac{5}{k}$$
The given equation relates the positive numbers \(m\), \(n\), and \(k\). Which equation correctly expresses \(m\) in terms of \(n\) and \(k\)?
questions.explanation:
Cross-multiply to eliminate the fractions.
$$\begin{aligned}3mk &= 20n \\ m &= \frac{20n}{3k}\end{aligned}$$

questions.stem: A population of bacteria doubles every 3 hours. If there are initially 500 bacteria, which of the following functions gives the population \(P\) after \(t\) hours?
questions.explanation:
Since the population doubles every 3 hours, the exponent must equal 1 when \(t = 3\). This means the exponent is \(\frac{t}{3}\), giving \(P(t) = 500 \cdot 2^{t/3}\).
Check: at \(t = 0\), \(P = 500\) ✓. At \(t = 3\), \(P = 500 \cdot 2^1 = 1000\) ✓ (doubled). At \(t = 6\), \(P = 500 \cdot 2^2 = 2000\) ✓ (doubled again).

questions.stem: Point \(O\) is the center of a circle. The measure of arc \(RS\) on this circle is \(124°\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ROS\)?
questions.explanation: A central angle and its intercepted arc have the same measure. Since arc \(RS\) measures \(124°\), angle \(ROS\) also measures \(124°\).

questions.stem: Priya started a new job with 40 hours of paid vacation time. She also accrues additional paid vacation hours at a constant rate each month. Priya did not use any of the vacation time, and at the end of 8 months she has a total of 136 paid vacation hours. Which equation can be used to find \(h\), the number of vacation hours Priya accrues each month?
questions.explanation:
Priya starts with 40 hours and accrues \(h\) hours per month for 8 months. Her total after 8 months is:
$$40 + 8h = 136$$

questions.stem: A cyclist travels at a speed of 480 meters per minute. What is the cyclist's speed, in kilometers per hour? (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
questions.explanation:
Convert meters per minute to kilometers per hour using the given conversion factor and the fact that there are 60 minutes in 1 hour.
$$480 \frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}} \times \frac{60 \text{ min}}{1 \text{ hr}} \times \frac{1 \text{ km}}{1{,}000 \text{ m}} = 28.8 \frac{\text{km}}{\text{hr}}$$

questions.stem: For what value of \(k\) does the equation \(kx^2 - 4x + 1 = 0\) have exactly one real solution?
questions.explanation:
A quadratic equation has exactly one real solution when its discriminant equals zero. For \(kx^2 - 4x + 1 = 0\), the discriminant is \(b^2 - 4ac = (-4)^2 - 4(k)(1) = 16 - 4k\).
$$16 - 4k = 0 \implies k = 4$$
When \(k = 4\), the equation \(4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0\) factors as \((2x - 1)^2 = 0\), giving exactly one solution \(x = \frac{1}{2}\). ✓

questions.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((3x^2 - 2x + 5) - (x^2 + 4x - 3)\)?
questions.explanation:
Distribute the negative sign and combine like terms.
$$\begin{aligned}&(3x^2 - 2x + 5) - (x^2 + 4x - 3) \\ &= 3x^2 - 2x + 5 - x^2 - 4x + 3 \\ &= 2x^2 - 6x + 8\end{aligned}$$
A common error is forgetting to distribute the negative sign to all terms in the second polynomial, especially the \(-3\), which becomes \(+3\).

questions.stem: $$3x + 2y = 17$$$$-3x + 5y = 11$$The solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of \(21y\)?
questions.explanation:
Add the two equations directly to eliminate \(x\).
$$\begin{aligned}3x + 2y &= 17 \\ + \quad (-3x + 5y) &= 11 \\ \hline 7y &= 28\end{aligned}$$
The question asks for \(21y\), which is \(3 \times 7y\).
$$21y = 3(7y) = 3(28) = 84$$

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = -(x - 2)^2 + 9\). What is the maximum value of \(f(x)\)?
questions.explanation:
The function is written in vertex form \(f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k\), where the vertex is at \((h, k)\). Here \(a = -1\), \(h = 2\), and \(k = 9\).
Since \(a = -1 < 0\), the parabola opens downward, so the vertex represents a maximum. The maximum value of \(f(x)\) is \(\mathbf{9}\), occurring at \(x = 2\).

questions.stem:
A city surveyed 480 randomly selected residents about their preferred activity at the local park. The results are shown in the table below.
Preferred ActivityNumber of Residents
Walking or jogging312
Team sports168
Total480
The city has 12,000 residents. Based on the survey results, how many more residents would be expected to prefer walking or jogging than team sports?
questions.explanation:
Find the expected number of residents who prefer each activity by applying the sample proportions to the full population of 12,000.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Walking/jogging: } \frac{312}{480} \times 12{,}000 &= 7{,}800 \\ \text{Team sports: } \frac{168}{480} \times 12{,}000 &= 4{,}200\end{aligned}$$
Subtract to find the expected difference.
$$7{,}800 - 4{,}200 = 3{,}600$$

questions.stem: In right triangle \(ABC\), angle \(B\) measures \(90°\) and angle \(A\) measures \(30°\). If the length of \(AC\) is \(12\), what is the area of triangle \(ABC\)?
questions.explanation:
Since angle \(B = 90°\) and angle \(A = 30°\), angle \(C = 60°\). Side \(AC\) is the hypotenuse. In a \(30°\)-\(60°\)-\(90°\) triangle, the shorter leg is half the hypotenuse and the longer leg is \(\sqrt{3}\) times the shorter leg.
$$BC = \frac{12}{2} = 6 \qquad AB = 6\sqrt{3}$$
The legs \(BC\) and \(AB\) are the base and height of the triangle.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 6\sqrt{3} = 18\sqrt{3}$$

questions.stem: $$f(x) = 45x + 1{,}200$$The function \(f\) gives the elevation \(f(x)\), in feet, of a hiker after climbing \(x\) flights of stairs from a starting elevation of 1,200 feet. What is the hiker's elevation, in feet, after climbing 16 flights of stairs?
questions.explanation:
Substitute \(x = 16\) into the function.
$$f(16) = 45(16) + 1{,}200 = 720 + 1{,}200 = 1{,}920$$

questions.stem: The graph of a quadratic function is shown. Which of the following could be an equation for the function?
questions.explanation:
The graph touches the \(x\)-axis at exactly one point, \((-2, 0)\), and does not cross it. This means the function has a double root at \(x = -2\).
A) \(y = (x-2)^2\) has a double root at \(x = 2\), not \(x = -2\). Eliminate A.
B) \(y = (x+2)^2\) has a double root at \(x = -2\) and a \(y\)-intercept of \(4\), which matches the graph. Keep B.
C) \(y = (x+2)(x-2)\) has two distinct \(x\)-intercepts at \(-2\) and \(2\) — the graph would cross the \(x\)-axis twice. Eliminate C.
D) \(y = (x+2)(x+4)\) has two distinct \(x\)-intercepts at \(-2\) and \(-4\). Eliminate D.


The correct answer is B.
